title: Orchestrated canary + automatic fallback for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce an orchestrated canary rollout controller for Dedicated GPU pools that coordinates LTS channel upgrades, autoscaler pauses, GPU-pool drain sequencing, and automatic fallback to the previous LTS when canary health gates fail. This ticket covers the control-plane coordinator (+ rollout DSL), drain policy templates, SLO-based gating, and integrations with the autoscaler and traffic router. Goal: reduce blast radius of upgrades while enabling predictable, low-latency rollouts for customers on Dedicated capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can start a canary rollout for a specified fleet and LTS channel with a single API call
Controller pauses autoscaling for canary pools and resumes post-rollout or on rollback
In the event of gate failure (latency P95 increase, error-rate spike, or node OOM), controller triggers automated rollback and drains newly-upgraded nodes back to old model variant without data-loss
Drain policy supports graceful connection handoff, KV-cache warmup on target nodes, and bounded in-flight token tail-latency
Operator can define custom gate predicates (metrics and log patterns) and an overall rollout timeout
Audit log entries created for each rollout step for compliance and postmortem
End-to-end integration tests that simulate mid-rollout autoscaler events and GPU pre-emption succeed in CI
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Dry-run - validate job manifests and drain templates against fleet metadata (no traffic)
Phase 1: Canary small slice (5% of traffic) on dedicated pool A with autoscaler frozen
Phase 2: Observe 30m with SLO gates (latency P95, error-rate, GPU-util variance). If gates pass, expand to 25%
Phase 3: Progressive expansion to 100% with scripted pauses (10m) and autoscaler unfreeze only after warmup windows
Rollback: Immediate abort and revert routing if any critical gate fires; re-seed old model variant and warm caches on rollback nodes before shifting traffic back
Post-rollout: automated acceptance job that verifies token-level cost delta and regression checks on eval prompt set
implementation_notes: Build a lightweight rollout coordinator service inside control plane (Go) integrating with existing fleet API
Provide a YAML DSL for rollout intent including LTS channel, candidate image, pool selectors, gate expressions, and drain template reference
Extend autoscaler with an API to ‘freeze’ scaling for targeted pools and query transient requests-in-flight
Drain template must expose knobs: drain_timeout, connection_grace_ms, kv_cache_warmup_steps, max_evacuate_concurrency
Routing layer must support gradual traffic shifts (weighted routing) and immediate cutover for rollback
Persist rollout state and events to audit-log store for compliance and postmortem analysis
testing_plan: Unit tests for DSL parsing and gate evaluation logic
Simulated canary scenarios in staging with synthetic traffic patterns (spike, slow requests, OOM) using chaos-job harness
Integration test: coordinator + autoscaler freeze + drain + routing rollback under pre-emption
Load test: measure token throughput and P95 during parallel rollouts across multiple pools
Security review: verify audit events and RBAC only allows whitelisted identities to initiate rollouts
risks: If autoscaler unfreeze timing is incorrect, newly-upgraded pools may be starved or cause overload elsewhere
KV-cache warmup delay could make early traffic latency appear degraded leading to false-positive gate failures
Complex rollback sequences risk duplicate in-flight requests unless connection handoff is handled precisely
Operator misconfiguration of gate thresholds could cause unnecessary rollbacks or unsafe rollouts
Missing observability on ephemeral drain steps could slow incident response
